name: Asymptotic Net
desc: Traces both families of asymptotic curves (zero normal curvature) for gridshell design. Asymptotic curves only exist where Gaussian curvature is negative; with AutoSpace the whole anticlastic region is filled with evenly spaced curves grown from one seed.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Seeds
inputs.desc: Seed vertex indices (optional with AutoSpace: the first one starts the net)

inputs.name: Step
inputs.desc: Integration step (0 = automatic: Spacing / 10, or from the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: MaxSteps
inputs.desc: Maximum steps per curve half (0 = automatic from the mesh size)

inputs.name: AutoSpace
inputs.desc: Fill the anticlastic region with evenly-spaced curves instead of tracing only from seeds

inputs.name: Spacing
inputs.desc: Target distance between adjacent curves (AutoSpace; 0 = automatic, bounding box / 30)

inputs.name: SeedPoints
inputs.desc: Seed points (nearest vertex is used); may be combined with Seeds

inputs.name: MaxCurves
inputs.desc: Cap on curves per family (AutoSpace, default 200)

outputs.name: Anticlastic
outputs.desc: Per input vertex: true where asymptotic directions exist (K < 0)

name: Chebyshev Net
desc: Constructs a Chebyshev net: equal edge lengths in both families everywhere. This is the kinematics of an elastic gridshell — a flat lattice of constant-length laths with rotating joints, bent into shape. Axis curves are geodesics from the seed; interior nodes are placed by the compass method.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.desc: Seed vertex index (net origin)

inputs.name: Direction
inputs.desc: First family direction at the seed

inputs.name: EdgeLength
inputs.desc: Lath segment length between joints

inputs.name: CountU
inputs.desc: Nodes per side of the seed, first family (default 10)

inputs.name: CountV
inputs.desc: Nodes per side of the seed, second family (default 10)

inputs.name: Angle
inputs.desc: Angle between families at the seed (default 90 degrees)

inputs.name: SeedPoint
inputs.desc: Net origin as a point (overrides Seed; nearest vertex is used)

outputs.name: Points
outputs.desc: Net nodes, one branch per row

outputs.name: NetMesh
outputs.desc: Quad mesh over the valid net cells

outputs.name: Angles
outputs.desc: Shear angle between the families at each node (degrees); locking occurs near 0 / 180

name: Conjugate Net
desc: Traces both families of principal curvature lines with even spacing, giving an approximate conjugate net — the curve layout whose quad cells can be planarized into a planar-quad (PQ) panelization of the surface.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Spacing
inputs.desc: Target distance between adjacent curves (0 = automatic, bounding box / 30)

inputs.name: Step
inputs.desc: Tracing step (0 = automatic: Spacing / 10)

inputs.name: MaxSteps
inputs.desc: Maximum steps per curve half (0 = automatic)

inputs.name: Seed
inputs.desc: First seed vertex (-1 = nearest the mesh centroid)

inputs.name: SeedPoint
inputs.desc: First seed as a point (overrides Seed)

inputs.name: MaxCurves
inputs.desc: Cap on curves per family (default 200)

name: Dynamic Relaxation
desc: Form finding by dynamic relaxation with kinetic damping: the mesh edges act as springs, optionally under gravity / point loads, soap-film tension and smoothing, and the system is integrated until it rests in equilibrium. Hanging models, pre-tensioned cable nets and quick minimal-surface-like relaxations of a gridshell mesh.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh (edges become springs)

inputs.name: Fixed
inputs.desc: Fixed vertex flags, one per input mesh vertex (empty = fix the boundary)

inputs.name: Stiffness
inputs.desc: Edge spring stiffness (default 1)

inputs.name: RestScale
inputs.desc: Rest length factor: 1 keeps edge lengths, < 1 pre-tensions the net (default 1)

inputs.name: Gravity
inputs.desc: Acceleration applied to every free vertex (default none; e.g. 0,0,-1 for a hanging model)

inputs.name: Loads
inputs.desc: Point load per input mesh vertex (one vector broadcasts)

inputs.name: Tension
inputs.desc: Soap-film (area minimization) strength (default 0)

inputs.name: Smoothness
inputs.desc: Laplacian smoothing strength (default 0)

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.desc: Maximum integration steps (default 2000)

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Convergence: residual force / applied force (default 1e-4)

outputs.name: Points
outputs.desc: Relaxed vertex positions (one per input mesh vertex)

outputs.name: Edges
outputs.desc: Springs in the order of the Forces output

outputs.name: Converged
outputs.desc: True when the residual dropped below the tolerance

name: Force Density Method
desc: Solves the equilibrium shape of a cable / strut net with the Force Density Method (linear, exact). Positive force densities give tension nets, negative ones compression shells. The Edges output lists the edge order used for per-edge force densities.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh (edges define the net)

inputs.name: ForceDensity
inputs.desc: Force density per edge (one value broadcasts; per-edge lists follow the Edges output order)

inputs.name: Loads
inputs.desc: Load vector per input mesh vertex (one vector broadcasts; coincident vertices share one load)

inputs.name: Fixed
inputs.desc: Fixed vertex flags, one per input mesh vertex (empty = fix the boundary)

outputs.name: Points
outputs.desc: Equilibrium vertex positions (one per input mesh vertex)

outputs.name: Edges
outputs.desc: Net edges in the order per-edge force densities are applied

outputs.name: Forces
outputs.desc: Axial force per edge (q * length; tension positive)

name: Gaussian Curvature
desc: Computes per-vertex Gaussian curvature via angle deficit over mixed Voronoi areas. Positive on domes, negative on saddles, zero on developable and boundary vertices. One value per input mesh vertex.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

name: Geodesic Net
desc: Traces straightest geodesics from seeds along given directions for gridshell design. Geodesics extend both ways from each seed; with AutoSpace one family fills the mesh with evenly spaced geodesics grown from the first seed and direction.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Seeds
inputs.desc: Seed vertex indices

inputs.name: Directions
inputs.desc: Initial direction per seed (last reused if fewer)

inputs.name: Step
inputs.desc: Integration step (0 = automatic)

inputs.name: MaxSteps
inputs.desc: Maximum steps per curve half (0 = automatic from the mesh size)

inputs.name: AutoSpace
inputs.desc: Fill the surface with evenly-spaced geodesics of one family, grown from the first seed and direction

inputs.name: Spacing
inputs.desc: Target distance between adjacent curves (AutoSpace; 0 = automatic)

inputs.name: SeedPoints
inputs.desc: Seed points (nearest vertex is used); may be combined with Seeds

inputs.name: MaxCurves
inputs.desc: Cap on the number of curves (AutoSpace, default 200)

name: Geodesic Path
desc: Shortest path on a mesh between two points: the straight lath you would lay from A to B. Graph search finds the route, curve shortening on the surface straightens it into a geodesic. Points are matched pairwise (the last is reused when lists differ).

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: From
inputs.desc: Start points

inputs.name: To
inputs.desc: End points

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Point spacing of the result (0 = automatic: half the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.desc: Maximum straightening passes per level (default 500)

name: Gridshell Analysis
desc: Linear static analysis of a lath network as a 3D beam frame. Laths become Euler-Bernoulli beams with the strip section, coupled at net crossings; supports are fixed points. Geometry is converted from the document units to metres internally, so E / Allowable are in Pa and Load in N/m whatever the model units. A first-order sanity check, not a full FE package.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Reference surface the net lies on

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Lath centerlines (net curves)

inputs.name: Joints
inputs.desc: Crossing points where laths are coupled (from Net Joints)

inputs.name: Supports
inputs.desc: Fixed support points

inputs.name: Load
inputs.desc: Force per unit length in N/m applied along every lath (default: 1 kN/m downward)

inputs.name: E
inputs.desc: Young's modulus in Pa (default 11 GPa ≈ timber)

inputs.name: Allowable
inputs.desc: Allowable combined stress in Pa (default 20 MPa)

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Lath width in model units (default 0.1)

inputs.name: Thickness
inputs.desc: Lath thickness in model units (default 0.01)

inputs.name: Upright
inputs.desc: Lath orientation, as in Lath Sweep

inputs.name: Scale
inputs.desc: Deformation display scale (default 1)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic)

inputs.name: MaxSegment
inputs.desc: Beam element size in model units (0 = automatic: twice the mesh edge length)

outputs.name: Deformed
outputs.desc: Deformed lath curves at the given display scale (one per input curve)

outputs.name: Utilization
outputs.desc: Stress utilization per lath element, one branch per lath (>1 fails)

outputs.name: LathUtilization
outputs.desc: Peak utilization per lath (one per input curve; wire into Lath Preview)

outputs.name: Axial
outputs.desc: Axial force per element in N (tension positive), one branch per lath

name: Lath Analysis
desc: Checks whether gridshell laths can be physically bent along curves on a mesh. Decomposes each curve into geodesic curvature (in-surface bend), normal curvature (out-of-surface bend), and geodesic torsion (twist), then compares the resulting bending strains of a rectangular strip against an allowable material strain.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Mesh the laths lie on

inputs.name: Laths
inputs.desc: Lath curves on the mesh (e.g. from Asymptotic Net or Geodesic Net)

inputs.name: Upright
inputs.desc: False: strip lies flat on the surface (geodesic gridshells). True: strip stands upright, perpendicular to the surface (asymptotic gridshells).

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Strip width, across the curve (default 0.1)

inputs.name: Thickness
inputs.desc: Strip thickness (default 0.01)

inputs.name: MaxStrain
inputs.desc: Allowable bending strain, e.g. sigma/E (default 0.005 ≈ timber; 0.002 steel, 0.008 GFRP)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic from the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: Window
inputs.desc: Arc length over which curvature is measured (0 = automatic: twice the mesh edge length). Larger windows smooth out facet-scale spikes

outputs.name: Buildable
outputs.desc: True if the lath stays within the strain limit (one per input curve)

outputs.name: MaxUtilization
outputs.desc: Peak strain / allowable strain per lath (>1 fails)

outputs.name: Utilization
outputs.desc: Strain utilization per point along each lath

outputs.name: NormalCurvature
outputs.desc: Out-of-surface bending per point (surface normal curvature along the lath; 0 on asymptotic curves)

outputs.name: Points
outputs.desc: Sample points the per-point values refer to

name: Lath Labels
desc: Assigns an ID to every lath, places a label point at each midpoint, and builds a CSV bill of materials (id, length, optional strain utilization from Lath Analysis). Wire the points and labels into a Text Tag component for display.

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Lath centerlines

inputs.name: Prefix
inputs.desc: ID prefix (default \"L\")

inputs.name: Utilization
inputs.desc: Optional per-lath utilization (from Lath Analysis / Gridshell Analysis) for the report

inputs.name: Start
inputs.desc: First ID number (default 0; use e.g. 100 for a second family)

name: Lath Preview
desc: Colors swept laths by utilization (e.g. from Lath Analysis or Gridshell Analysis): green within limits, yellow near the limit, red beyond it.

inputs.name: Laths
inputs.desc: Swept lath meshes (from Lath Sweep)

inputs.name: Utilization
inputs.desc: Per-lath utilization values (1.0 = at the limit)

name: Lath Segment
desc: Splits laths into pieces that fit stock material length, keeping cuts away from net crossings. Consecutive pieces overlap by the splice length, and half-lap splice notch solids (Ne for the upstream piece, Ns for the downstream one) are built at each cut: subtract them from the swept pieces with Mesh Difference.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Reference surface

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Lath centerlines

inputs.name: StockLength
inputs.desc: Available material length (default 3)

inputs.name: Margin
inputs.desc: Minimum distance between a cut and a joint (default 0.05)

inputs.name: Joints
inputs.desc: Crossing points to avoid (from Net Joints; only those on each lath are used)

inputs.name: SpliceLength
inputs.desc: Half-lap splice overlap length (default 0.15)

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Lath width (default 0.1)

inputs.name: Thickness
inputs.desc: Lath thickness (default 0.01)

inputs.name: Upright
inputs.desc: Lath orientation, as in Lath Sweep

inputs.name: Clearance
inputs.desc: Fit clearance (default 0)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic from the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: Offset
inputs.desc: Gap between the surface and the nearest lath face, as in Lath Sweep (default 0)

outputs.name: Segments
outputs.desc: Lath pieces, one branch per input lath

outputs.name: Cuts
outputs.desc: Cut points, one branch per input lath

outputs.name: NotchesEnd
outputs.desc: Splice notches for the upstream piece at each cut

outputs.name: NotchesStart
outputs.desc: Splice notches for the downstream piece at each cut

outputs.name: Lengths
outputs.desc: Piece lengths, one branch per input lath

name: Lath Sweep
desc: Extrudes curves lying on a mesh into solid laths with a rectangular profile. The profile rides in the surface frame: flat laths hug the surface (geodesic gridshells), upright laths stand on edge (asymptotic gridshells). Outputs stay index-aligned with the input curves (null where a curve could not be swept).

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Reference surface the curves lie on

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Lath centerlines on the surface

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Profile width across the curve (default 0.1)

inputs.name: Thickness
inputs.desc: Profile thickness through the strip (default 0.01)

inputs.name: Upright
inputs.desc: False: strip lies flat on the surface. True: strip stands upright on edge

inputs.name: Offset
inputs.desc: Gap between the surface and the nearest strip face (default 0)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic from the mesh edge length)

outputs.name: Laths
outputs.desc: Swept lath solids as closed meshes, one per input curve

outputs.name: Centerlines
outputs.desc: Strip centerline per lath (lifted by the offset and half the depth)

outputs.name: Frames
outputs.desc: Start frame per lath (X along the lath, Z along the surface normal)

name: Lath Unroll
desc: Unrolls lath strips to flat 2D cutting patterns. Each pattern is isometric to the swept strip (exact per triangle), so it is ready for CNC/laser cutting. Patterns are laid out in a row with the given gap; closed laths are opened at their seam. Outputs stay index-aligned with the input curves (null where a curve failed).

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Reference surface the curves lie on

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Lath centerlines on the surface

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Strip width (default 0.1)

inputs.name: Upright
inputs.desc: Lath orientation, as in Lath Sweep

inputs.name: Gap
inputs.desc: Gap between laid-out patterns (default 0.05)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic from the mesh edge length)

outputs.name: Patterns
outputs.desc: Closed flat cutting patterns, laid out in a row

outputs.name: FlatMeshes
outputs.desc: Triangulated flat pattern per lath (preview / nesting)

name: Mean Curvature
desc: Computes per-vertex mean curvature via the cotangent Laplacian (mixed Voronoi areas, consistent with Gaussian Curvature). Boundary vertices are zero. One value per input mesh vertex.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

outputs.name: HN
outputs.desc: Mean curvature normal vector per vertex (length |H|)

name: Mesh Cleanup
desc: Heals a mesh for analysis: welds coincident vertices (within a tolerance), removes degenerate and duplicate faces, reduces collapsed faces, and unifies face winding. Mite components weld exactly coincident vertices on their own; run this first on meshes with near-coincident vertices, slivers or mixed winding (joins, booleans, imports).

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Vertex weld distance (0 = automatic: 1e-6 of the average edge length)

inputs.name: UnifyWinding
inputs.desc: Make face winding consistent

outputs.name: Map
outputs.desc: Cleaned vertex index for each input vertex

name: Mesh Colour Map
desc: Colours a mesh by per-vertex values in one step (no Bounds / Remap / Gradient chain). Diverging palettes are centred on zero, which suits signed curvature: blue negative, white zero, red positive.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Values
inputs.desc: One value per mesh vertex (e.g. K, H, K1)

inputs.name: Domain
inputs.desc: Value range to map (empty = automatic, robust 2%..98% percentiles)

inputs.name: Palette
inputs.desc: 0 = diverging blue-white-red (centred on 0), 1 = viridis-like sequential, 2 = traffic light (green-yellow-red)

name: Mesh Isocurves
desc: Extracts isocurves of a per-vertex scalar field (curvature, utilization, height, ...) at the given levels. Wire Gaussian Curvature with level 0 to outline the anticlastic regions where asymptotic laths can exist. One branch per level.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Values
inputs.desc: One value per input mesh vertex

inputs.name: Levels
inputs.desc: Iso levels (default 0)

inputs.name: Smooth
inputs.desc: Output smooth interpolated curves instead of polylines (default false)

name: Minimal Surface
desc: Finds a minimal surface with fixed boundaries by iterating exact cotangent Laplace solves (each iteration freezes the weights and solves the sparse linear system). Leave Fixed empty to fix the mesh boundary.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Fixed
inputs.desc: Fixed vertex flags, one per input mesh vertex (empty = fix the boundary)

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.desc: Max weight-update iterations (default 20)

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Convergence: max vertex move per iteration as a fraction of the mesh size (default 1e-8)

outputs.name: Residual
outputs.desc: Max vertex movement in the last iteration

name: Net Joints
desc: Finds the crossings between the two lath families of a gridshell net and builds lap-joint notch solids for each crossing. Boolean-subtract the notches from the swept laths (Mesh Difference) to fabricate the joints.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Reference surface the net lies on

inputs.name: CurvesA
inputs.desc: First lath family

inputs.name: CurvesB
inputs.desc: Second lath family (empty: crossings within family A)

inputs.name: Width
inputs.desc: Lath profile width (default 0.1)

inputs.name: Thickness
inputs.desc: Lath profile thickness (default 0.01)

inputs.name: Upright
inputs.desc: False: laths lie flat (lap notch). True: laths stand upright (egg-crate slot)

inputs.name: Offset
inputs.desc: Gap between the surface and the nearest lath face (default 0)

inputs.name: Lap
inputs.desc: Notched fraction of the profile depth (default 0.5 = half-lap)

inputs.name: Clearance
inputs.desc: Fit clearance added to each notch side (default 0)

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Maximum gap accepted as a crossing (0 = automatic)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic from the mesh edge length)

outputs.name: Planes
outputs.desc: Joint frame per crossing (X along family A, Z along the surface normal)

outputs.name: Angles
outputs.desc: Crossing angle between the laths, in degrees

outputs.name: NotchesA
outputs.desc: Notch solids to subtract from family A laths

outputs.name: NotchesB
outputs.desc: Notch solids to subtract from family B laths

outputs.name: IndexA
outputs.desc: Index of the family A curve at each crossing

outputs.name: IndexB
outputs.desc: Index of the family B curve at each crossing (a family A index when CurvesB is empty)

name: Net Topology
desc: Turns a two-family lath net into a structural graph: unique nodes at the crossings and one member per lath piece between consecutive crossings (free tails included). Feed Nodes / Members to a structural package (e.g. Karamba) or use the node schedule for fabrication.

inputs.name: CurvesA
inputs.desc: First lath family

inputs.name: CurvesB
inputs.desc: Second lath family

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Maximum gap accepted as a crossing (0 = automatic)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Chord deviation for curve sampling (0 = automatic: 1/500 of the net size)

inputs.name: MinLength
inputs.desc: Drop members (e.g. free tails) shorter than this (default 0)

outputs.name: Start
outputs.desc: Node index at each member start (-1 = free end)

outputs.name: End
outputs.desc: Node index at each member end (-1 = free end)

outputs.name: Lath
outputs.desc: Input lath of each member: family A indices, then family B continuing

outputs.name: NodeLaths
outputs.desc: Per node: the two lath indices crossing there

name: Planarize Mesh
desc: Iterative quad planarization by projecting vertices onto per-face best-fit planes. Set Strength to 0 to only measure planarity without moving anything.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input quad mesh

inputs.name: Iterations
inputs.desc: Max iterations (default 100)

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Convergence tolerance on the max face deviation, model units (default 1e-6)

inputs.name: Fixed
inputs.desc: Fixed vertex flags (one per input mesh vertex)

inputs.name: Strength
inputs.desc: Step strength per iteration 0..1 (default 1; 0 = measure only)

outputs.name: Deviation
outputs.desc: Planarity deviation per face (max distance of a corner from the best-fit plane)

name: Principal Curvature
desc: Computes principal curvatures and directions per vertex (Rusinkiewicz per-face second-fundamental-form fit, tensor-smoothed over R vertex rings). Outputs are one item per input mesh vertex, ready for Mesh Colours.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Radius
inputs.desc: Smoothing radius in vertex rings (1 = none, default 2)

outputs.name: Normals
outputs.desc: Vertex normals used for the tangent frames ((D1, D2, N) is right-handed)

name: Pull To Mesh
desc: Projects curves and points onto a mesh by closest point, so hand-drawn or edited lath layouts can feed Lath Analysis, Lath Sweep and Net Joints like traced ones. Optionally fairs the pulled curves on the surface to remove facet kinks.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Target mesh

inputs.name: Curves
inputs.desc: Curves to pull (optional)

inputs.name: Points
inputs.desc: Points to pull (optional)

inputs.name: Sampling
inputs.desc: Curve sampling length along the curve (0 = automatic: half the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: Smoothing
inputs.desc: On-surface fairing passes for the pulled curves (default 0)

outputs.name: Curves
outputs.desc: Pulled curves (smooth interpolated, on the mesh)

outputs.name: Normals
outputs.desc: Smooth mesh normal at each pulled point

name: Curvature Streamlines
desc: Traces lines of curvature along the maximum or minimum principal direction, from seed vertices / points or filling the mesh with evenly spaced lines (AutoSpace).

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Seeds
inputs.desc: Seed vertex indices

inputs.name: Step
inputs.desc: Integration step (0 = automatic from the mesh edge length)

inputs.name: MaxSteps
inputs.desc: Maximum steps per curve half (0 = automatic from the mesh size)

inputs.name: MaxDir
inputs.desc: Use max curvature direction (true) or min (false)

inputs.name: SeedPoints
inputs.desc: Seed points (nearest vertex is used); may be combined with Seeds

inputs.name: AutoSpace
inputs.desc: Fill the mesh with evenly spaced lines grown from the first seed

inputs.name: Spacing
inputs.desc: Target distance between adjacent lines (AutoSpace; 0 = automatic)

inputs.name: MaxCurves
inputs.desc: Cap on the number of lines (AutoSpace, default 200)

name: Umbilics
desc: Finds umbilical points, where the two principal curvatures are equal and the principal directions are undefined. Curve networks rotate wildly around umbilics — use this to place net seeds deliberately or to mask regions before tracing.

inputs.name: Mesh
inputs.desc: Input mesh

inputs.name: Tolerance
inputs.desc: Relative |k1-k2| tolerance (default 0.05)

outputs.name: Indices
outputs.desc: Umbilical vertex indices (of the input mesh)

outputs.name: Mask
outputs.desc: Per input vertex: true where umbilical
